Characters

Core holds the most used characters; the other tabs hold the rest of what the families map, by group (alternates, ligatures and other glyphs with no character of their own are not shown). One cell each. With more than one font on, each cell stacks them in the order of the buttons (in the Code tab, Nunuïko first), in the colours of the key (overlaid in Overlay). Grey guides mark each font’s baseline and cap height, and the edges of the advance for the monospaced fonts. A font that lacks a character leaves its line in the cell empty. Accents are shown on a no-break space.

Tabular figures: figures and the signs set with them, with tabular figures on (tnum), as in tables and columns of numbers. Nunuïko and Display give the footed 1 here; Nunuïkode’s figures are all one width anyway. No non-stock tint: these are separate glyphs.

Non-stock characters, drawn differently from the stock font (Nunito, or Nunito Sans for Display), have a tinted cell; hover one to see what each family changed. Nunuïkode counts Nunuïko’s changes and its own code edits, not the moving and condensing every glyph gets to fit the cell.

Waterfall: the l / I / 1 triplet leads each line: it has to stay readable down to 9 px. Each size sets every font on, one row each.

Weight ramp: the same line at each named weight, every font on, one row each.

Every change from the stock font, newest last, for each family switched on; the full record is in each family’s GLYPHLOG.md.

G variants

The default G (a straight drop under the bar) and the alternate, the round G (stylistic set 3, ss03). Fonts without an ss03 show their default G twice.

Text

Typography is the craft of endowing human language with a durable visual form. Quick zephyrs blow, vexing daft Jim; the five boxing wizards jump quickly. Grumpy wizards make toxic brew for the jovial queen — 1,234.56 kg at 09:41, “quoted”, ‘single’, (parenthesised) and [bracketed]. Ægir’s fjord, Łódź, Ýmir, Ğöksu, naïve café, Schöne Grüße, Ящик, Ёжик.

import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

// Parse a config file; fall back to defaults on any error.
export async function loadConfig(path: string): Promise<Config> {
  try {
    const raw = await readFile(path, "utf8");
    const cfg = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<Config>;
    return { ...defaults, ...cfg, retries: cfg.retries ?? 3 };
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn(`config: ${path} unreadable (${err})`);
    return defaults;
  }
}
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    sensor: str
    value: float
    ok: bool = True


def average(readings: list[Reading], floor: float = 0.0) -> float | None:
    """Mean of the good readings at or above floor, or None."""
    good = [r.value for r in readings if r.ok and r.value >= floor]
    return sum(good) / len(good) if good else None  # 0 readings -> None

/* buttons: one size, three looks */
:root { --ink: #1C1C1E; --accent: #2F62A6; --radius: 8px; }

.btn { display: inline-flex; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border-radius: var(--radius); }
.btn:hover, .btn:focus-visible { color: var(--ink); outline: 2px solid rgb(47 98 166 / .4); }
.btn[aria-pressed="true"] > svg { transform: rotate(-90deg); }

@media (max-width: 640px) { .btn { width: calc(100% - 2 * 16px); } }

-- users with at least one order this year, busiest first
SELECT u.id, u.email, COUNT(o.id) AS orders, SUM(o.total) AS spent
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.status <> 'void'
WHERE u.created_at >= '2026-01-01' AND u.email LIKE '%@example.com'
GROUP BY u.id, u.email
HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0
ORDER BY spent DESC
LIMIT 10;
<template>
  <ul class="list">
    <li v-for="item in visible" :key="item.id" :class="{ done: item.done }">
      <input type="checkbox" v-model="item.done" />
      {{ item.title }} <small v-if="item.due">{{ formatDate(item.due) }}</small>
    </li>
  </ul>
  <button @click="showAll = !showAll">{{ showAll ? 'Hide done' : 'Show all' }}</button>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref, computed } from 'vue';

const props = defineProps({ items: { type: Array, required: true } });
const showAll = ref(false);
const visible = computed(() => props.items.filter((i) => showAll.value || !i.done));
const formatDate = (d) => new Date(d).toLocaleDateString('en-CA');
</script>

<style scoped>
.list { display: grid; gap: 4px; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
.done { color: #8E8E93; text-decoration: line-through; }
</style>

Texture healing

Next to a narrow letter (i j l r t f I), a wide letter (m w M W A O Q V …) borrows up to 60 units of its space, and the narrow letter steps aside. Cells stay 600 wide, so columns still line up. It is the calt feature; top row on, bottom row off.
